sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1990. Esquisse du parler des Balobo. In: Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale (Études Aequatoria 8), 239-254. Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria. (Glottolog ref 68000; Glottolog's most extensive description for liki1240)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. I 'Phonologie' (pp. 239-240, page images read): 7 oral vowels, consonant remarks (gb/kp~kw, dz for l before i, N+voiceless C, labiodental nasal mw), glide, devocalisation of o, elision/coalescence 'avec ou sans perte de tonalité', vowel harmony; the only prosodic sentence is 'la tonologie est comparativement au Bantu commun du type normal' (p. 240). No mention of accent/stress in the rest of the sketch (pp. 241-254, morphology) nor in the volume's Conclusion (pp. 274-275). Variety: parler balobo of Mbongo village, Zone de Bomongo; informant Lutu Litebe.

sources.citation: Donzo Bunza Yugia, Jean-Pierre. 2015. Langues bantoues de l'entre Congo-Ubangi (RD Congo): documentation, reconstruction, classification et contacts avec les langues oubanguiennes. Thèse de doctorat, ULB / UGent.

sources.note: Balobo ('C314 Balobo') appears only in lexicostatistic trees and subgroup lists (pp. 135-139); it is not one of the ten languages described, so no Balobo phonology or prosody.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André & Bonzoi Mwamakasa. 2008. Aux sources du lingála: cas du mbenga de Mankanza – Nouvel Anvers. African Study Monographs Suppl. 38: 1-93.

sources.note: Balobo mentioned only ethno-historically (pp. 6-9); the phonology is of Mbenga, not Balobo; no stress statement relevant to liki1240.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre (Études Aequatoria 8) -- Introduction générale pp. 1-11 and Conclusion pp. 274-275
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No general prosodic statement for the riverine languages; intro p. 2 notes 'Les Likila parlent la même langue que ces deux premiers groupes [Baloi, Bato ba loi], avec certes de légères différences' (identity remark only). (A penultimate-lengthening remark at p. ~69 belongs to the Libobi sketch, not Balobo.)

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1951. La tonologie des parlers bantous du Nord-Ouest du Congo belge. Bulletin des Séances, Institut Royal Colonial Belge 22(4): 900-919.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tone typology only (riverains of Ubangi/Congo/Ngiri = 'tonologie type lingála': word tonology not influenced by neighbouring words); no stress/accent statement; Balobo not named individually.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1949. Dialectgroepen in het Ngiri-gebied. Aequatoria 12: 87-94.
